newsitem.title: USA: Sonic sees Q2 EPS below analysts' views.
newsitem.headline: Sonic sees Q2 EPS below analysts' views.

text.p: Sonic Corp on Monday said that while it expects to report fiscal second quarter ended February 28 share earnings that are about 10 percent higher than the year ago's $0.21, they will be below analyst estimates of $0.25-$0.27.

The company attributes this primarily to slower-than-scheduled new drive-in openings during the quarter and the fact that drive-ins in new markets are taking longer than originally estimated to reach sales and profit goals.

But Sonic said that as a whole (franchise and company operations combined) it continues to perform well with average unit sales volumes for the second quarter, on a preliminary basis, having increased eight to nine percent over the year-ago period. The company expects to announce final financial results for its fiscal second quarter on April 14, 1997.

"Our business concept is healthy and our system's sales and profitability continue to grow," said Clifford Hudson, president and chief executive officer, "but we are confronted in our company drive-ins with a dual challenge of limited market penetration in new markets on one hand and delays in the opening of new company-operated drive-ins on the other. The result is fewer than planned drive-ins to generate profits and less additional market penetration to drive incremental sales of existing drive-ins in these new markets.

"With the impact of these developments applicable to at least some portion of the remainder of our fiscal year ending August 31, we believe that our earnings growth for fiscal 1997 will be around 10 percent. May and June will be important months for us, particularly from the standpoint of opening new company drive-ins."
